formulas.name: Calculator constants
where: Fraction of HBM reserved for activations + workspace + paging fragmentation (10% → 90% utilization; vLLM default is 92%).
NVLink fan-out ceiling (HGX/DGX). Useful ceiling is min(TP_CAP, Y_max).
DJL TRT-LLM token-budget hint midpoint: mnbt ≈ α × B × ISL, α ∈ [0.1, 0.2].
Prefill MFU midpoint (~30–50% band) for closed-form prefill throughput.
Decode MFU midpoint (~5–15% band). Kept for reference; decode tput now derived from stepTime.
Bytes per element by dtype; INT4 stored as 0.5 so multiplication never truncates a param count.
Sarathi-Serve §5.1 token-budget bands; single source of truth shared by picker and sweep grid.
formulas.description: Tunable constants used across the calculator: HBM headroom, NVLink TP ceiling, DJL token-budget α, MFU midpoints, dtype byte costs, Sarathi-Serve bands.
formulas.derivation: ACT_OVERHEAD=0.10 is a vLLM-style headroom (intentionally conservative vs vLLM's 92% default). TP_CAP=8 is the NVLink fan-out of a standard HGX/DGX node. α=0.15 is the DJL TRT-LLM 'sensible band' midpoint. PREFILL_MFU=0.40 and DECODE_MFU=0.10 are reference §0.3 band midpoints synthesized from DeepSeek-V3 (~34% prefill / ~7% decode on FP8 H800), 'Investigation of FP8 Across Accelerators' (square GEMM ~59% FP8 peak; thin GEMM <1%), Sarathi-Serve, and Databricks (which reports MBU not MFU for decode). SARATHI_BANDS = {512 strict, 1024 default, 1536 LLaMA-70B PP variant, 2048 relaxed cap, 4096, 8192} — verbatim from Sarathi-Serve §5.1 plus throughput extensions; one constant guarantees the picker and sweep grid agree.

formulas.name: Weight memory (total HBM stream)
where: Total params in billions (for MoE: all experts — all must sit in HBM regardless of routing).
Total weight bytes streamed from HBM per step.
formulas.description: Aggregate weight memory. TP shards it across GPUs, but the aggregate matters because aggregate HBM BW also scales with the shard count.
formulas.derivation: params_b_total is in billions to match the data table; multiply by 1e9 once here. Total (not active) is used because MoE routing does not shrink HBM footprint — all experts must be resident even if only a few execute per token. Compute uses active params via stepTime's paramCount_active.

formulas.name: KV bytes per token (MHA / GQA / MQA)
where: Number of KV heads (n_kv < n_heads for GQA; n_kv = 1 for MQA; n_kv = n_heads for MHA).
K and V tensors cached separately.
formulas.description: KV cache bytes per token per sequence for standard attention. The factor of 2 is K + V; reducing n_kv is what GQA / MQA compress.
formulas.derivation: Reference §3: each layer caches one K and one V of shape (n_kv × d_head) per token in dtype b_kv; multiply by L for the model. GQA compresses by reducing n_kv vs n_heads (Llama-3-70B: 8 KV heads vs 64 attention heads → 8× smaller KV than dense MHA). MQA pushes n_kv to 1.

formulas.name: KV bytes per token (MLA)
where: Latent (kv_lora_rank) dimension of the low-rank KV compression.
RoPE key dimension (qk_rope_head_dim) carried alongside the latent.
formulas.description: KV bytes per token for Multi-head Latent Attention (DeepSeek-V2/V3). One shared low-rank latent plus a small RoPE key, cached once across all heads.
formulas.derivation: MLA is structurally different (reference §3 table): one low-rank latent of size d_c plus one RoPE key of size d_rope, shared across heads. No factor of 2 (single cached tensor, not K+V separately), no n_kv, no d_head multiplier. Field names match DeepSeek HF config. This is why DeepSeek-V3 (671B total) has a smaller per-token KV than Llama-3-70B despite being ~10× larger.

formulas.name: Roofline ridge-point batch (B_crit)
where: Precision-adjusted peak FLOPs (FP8 path only when both operands FP8 + HW support; else FP16/BF16 rate).
Weight and activation precision in bits.
formulas.description: Batch size where the MLP kernel flips from memory-bound to compute-bound. Below B_crit, FLOPs idle; above it, latency grows linearly with B.
formulas.derivation: Standard AI threshold (reference §1, Scaling Book inference Q5): ridge of the roofline is where compute time equals memory time per matmul. bits_w/bits_act is the book's rule that int8/fp8 doubles B_crit. FP8 tensor cores fire only when both operands are FP8 + HW supports it; asymmetric precision rides FP16 path and shifts only via bits_w/bits_act. The N_total/N_active factor is the Scaling Book MoE sparsity correction: weights stream all experts each step while compute scales only with active experts, so the ridge shifts right by that ratio. Example: DeepSeek-V3 on H100 BF16/BF16, dense B_crit=295, sparsity 671/37≈18.135 → B_crit_MoE≈5347.

formulas.name: Per-step decode latency (per-kernel form)
where: KV bytes per token per sequence.
Per-sequence KV occupancy; we use PEAK seq = ISL + OSL (last decode step).
Aggregate HBM bandwidth and compute across all GPUs.
Total HBM weight stream (all experts for MoE).
Per-token active parameters (= N_total for dense).
formulas.description: Attention kernel (always memory-bound on KV) plus MLP kernel (max of weight-load vs compute). Each layer runs these as separate sequential CUDA kernels, so they add per step.
formulas.derivation: Reference §4 / Scaling Book. Attention and MLP are separate sequential kernels per layer → per-step time sums. Attention AI is ~1 at decode (no compute roof), so pure HBM-BW on the KV stream. The MLP max picks the slower of weight-load (W/BW, constant in B) and compute (2BN/FLOPs, linear in B). MoE contract: W uses total params; compute term uses active. PEAK seq (ISL+OSL) — not mean — because SLAs bound EVERY step and the last decode step is the worst. Sizing against the mean fits batches that meet TBT on average but blow SLO at end-of-decode.

formulas.name: Aggregate decode throughput
where: Aggregate tokens/sec emitted by the fleet.
formulas.description: Vendor-headline tok/s, not per-user rate. Autoregressive invariant: one new token per active sequence per step, so fleet tps = B / T_step.
formulas.derivation: B tokens land per step → tps = B / T_step. Inherits stepTime's regimes: roughly linear in B below B_crit, then saturates at FLOPs/(2N) above (B cancels asymptotically because T_step is itself linear in B). Per-user rate is 1/T_step — strictly smaller. Delegating to stepTime keeps a single source of truth for the per-kernel breakdown.

formulas.name: Cost per million output tokens
where: USD price per GPU per hour.
Aggregate decode tokens/sec at the operating point.
formulas.description: Unit conversion closing the third axis of the Pareto surface (latency × throughput × $/Mtok). Fleet $/hr ÷ fleet tokens/hr, scaled to per-million.
formulas.derivation: Fleet cost = p × n_gpus $/hr; emission rate = tps × 3600 tok/hr; $/tok = (p × n_gpus) / (tps × 3600); scale by 1e6. Edge cases: price=null → null (renders '—'); tps=0 → Infinity (caller masks); price=0 → 0 (free hardware = free tokens).

formulas.name: Largest batch meeting TBT SLO (b_slo)
formulas.expr_tex: \begin{aligned} B_{\text{ridge}} &= \frac{W \cdot \text{FLOPs}}{2 N_{\text{active}} \cdot \text{BW}} \\ B_a &= \frac{(T_{\text{slo}} - W/\text{BW}) \cdot \text{BW}}{K_{\text{tok}} \cdot S} \\ B_b &= \frac{T_{\text{slo}}}{K_{\text{tok}} S / \text{BW} + 2 N_{\text{active}} / \text{FLOPs}} \\ B_{\text{slo}} &= \begin{cases} B_a & B_a \le B_{\text{ridge}} \\ B_b & B_b \ge B_{\text{ridge}} \\ B_{\text{ridge}} & \text{otherwise} \end{cases} \end{aligned}
where: Total weight stream and active params.
KV per token and peak seq (ISL + OSL).
Candidate solutions in the MLP weight-load and MLP compute regimes.
formulas.description: Largest batch keeping every decode step under the TBT SLO. Solves stepTime piecewise across its two MLP regimes; the binding answer is the candidate that lands in its own regime.
formulas.derivation: T_step is piecewise-linear in B with MLP-ridge crossover at B_ridge = (W·FLOPs)/(2N·BW). Below the ridge W/BW dominates; above, 2BN/FLOPs does. Each regime gives a linear equation; the binding answer is the candidate whose B sits in its own regime. If both straddle the ridge, the SLO is met exactly at B_ridge. B_ridge is NOT B_crit — they coincide for symmetric precision (BF16/BF16) but diverge for FP8/FP8 (B_ridge≈α, B_crit≈2α) because Scaling Book's stepTime omits activation streaming. Replacing B_ridge with bCrit() would silently report falsely permissive values for FP8/FP8. We also flag 'attention' as the binder if attention alone exceeds the budget. PEAK seq makes this SLO-conservative (worst step, not average) — the right framing for any p99-style SLA.

formulas.name: Largest batch fitting KV in HBM (b_kv)
where: Total weight stream (all experts for MoE).
KV bytes per token (from kvPerToken for the right attention variant).
formulas.description: Largest batch that fits the KV cache in HBM after weights and activation headroom. Uses peak occupancy so the bound never OOMs mid-generation.
formulas.derivation: Reference §3 / §5: usable HBM for KV = HBM × (1 − ACT_OVERHEAD) − W; KV per sequence = K_tok × peak_seq. ISL+OSL is the conservative choice because KV grows monotonically through decode — last step is worst case for OOM. This function owns the kvPerToken call internally so callers can't silently mis-apply the MHA formula to MLA. Compute sparsity does NOT shrink HBM footprint; W is the total stream.

formulas.name: Useful TP ceiling (Y_max)
where: FFW hidden dim (d_model and L cancel in the derivation; only d_ff survives).
Hardware HBM-to-ICI BW ratio (H100 ≈ 3.7, A100 ≈ 3.4, TPU v5e ≈ 8).
formulas.description: Max useful TP degree per replica before ICI all-reduce dominates per-step decode latency. Past Y_max, more TP does not cut step time.
formulas.derivation: Reference §6 (Scaling Book): per-layer FFW weight stream T_HBM = 2DF/(Y·W_hbm); per-layer activation all-reduce T_ICI = 2BD/W_ici. The crossover T_ICI > T_HBM simplifies (D cancels both sides; L scales both equally) to Y > d_ff / (B · β) — only d_ff survives. Returns +∞ if ici_bw_gbs is missing ('no constraint modelled'); caller still applies TP_CAP and memory-fit ceilings. This is a latency-usefulness ceiling, not a hard limit — exceeding it means more TP doesn't help (and may hurt), not that it crashes.

formulas.name: Recommend TP × PP × replicas
where: Smallest TP in {1,2,4,8} that fits the per-GPU shard.
Pipeline stages used when no TP in {1,2,4,8} fits: TP=8 per stage, PP = ceil(W / (8 × HBM_per_gpu_usable)).
formulas.description: Two-ceiling parallelism recommender. Smallest TP that fits the memory shard; falls back to TP=8 × PP when even TP=8 won't fit; surfaces Y_max as a soft diagnostic.
formulas.derivation: Scan {1,2,4,8} (NVLink-aligned, ngpus-bounded); pick the smallest TP whose shard W/TP fits HBM_per_gpu × (1 − ACT_OVERHEAD). Replicas = floor(ngpus / TP). No fit → use TP=8 per stage and PP = ceil(W / (8 · HBM_per_gpu_usable)). We do NOT force TP down to Y_max — if memory needs TP=4 we honor that even if Y_max=2 — but surface a diagnostic so users know TP=4 was memory-driven, not latency-driven. Useful cap = min(TP_CAP, ngpus, floor(Y_max)). Memory-fit is hard; Y_max is soft.

formulas.name: Recommended max_num_batched_tokens
formulas.expr_tex: \text{mnbt} = \min_{c \in \text{SARATHI\_BANDS}} \big\{ c : c \geq \max(1024,\, \alpha \cdot B \cdot \text{ISL}) \big\},\quad \text{capped at 2048 if TBT} \leq 30\text{ ms}
formulas.description: Starting value for vLLM's --max-num-batched-tokens — the per-step token budget that gates how much prefill can backfill alongside decode. Picked from the Sarathi-Serve verified bands instead of a free-form integer so the analytical recommendation matches a configuration the paper actually measured.
formulas.derivation: Sarathi-Serve §5.1 shows that strict-TBT deployments (≤30 ms) should run a small chunk (~512) to protect per-token latency, while relaxed deployments (~100 ms TBT) can run 2048 to recover prefill throughput. DJL's TRT-LLM tuning guide gives an upper-bound hint of α·B·ISL with α ∈ [0.1, 0.2] (we use 0.15, the midpoint). The picker takes max(1024, hint) and walks the verified band list upward, then applies the strict cap of 2048 if TBT ≤ 30 ms. Returning the band label ('strict' vs 'relaxed') lets the UI explain which regime the recommendation came from.

formulas.name: Per-chip prefill throughput
where: Per-chip peak FLOPs (FP8 path needs both operands FP8 + HW support).
Per-token active params (matmul FLOPs = 2 · N_active per token).
Self-attention FLOPs per token (Q·Kᵀ + attn·V over preceding ISL/2 tokens × 2 matmuls, causally averaged).
formulas.description: Tokens/sec/chip for prefill at the operating MFU. Feeds pdRatio. B does not appear because per-step work and tokens generated both scale linearly in B, so B cancels.
formulas.derivation: Per-token FLOPs has two components: matmul (QKVO + FFW) = 2 · N_active per token (Scaling Book §6 convention) plus self-attention (causally averaged) = 2 · ISL · d_model · L. Attention share at d_model=8192, L=80: ~1% at ISL=2k, ~8% at ISL=8k (Scaling Book worked example), ~30% at ISL=32k, >70% at ISL=128k (MFU convention itself breaks down). PREFILL_MFU=0.40 anchors at 'decently-batched chunked prefill' (~2k chunks); achieved MFU swings ~30% at 512 chunks to ~50–60% at 8k+. That swing is the dominant source of pdRatio's order-of-magnitude band. FP8 selection rule mirrors bCrit's.

formulas.name: Prefill:Decode replica ratio
where: Decode tokens/sec/chip from stepTime/throughputAtB at operating B.
formulas.description: Prefill:decode chip ratio for disaggregated sizing. Order-of-magnitude correct; expect ±2× vs production sizers (DistServe / Splitwise / Mooncake use SLO-bound simulators).
formulas.derivation: Reference §5.2 / DistServe (OSDI '24) §4 throughput-based form: n_p = ceil(R / prefill_goodput), n_d = ceil(R / decode_goodput) → P:D = decode_goodput / prefill_goodput. Expand goodput as req/s/chip = tokens/sec/chip ÷ tokens-per-req: prefill_goodput = prefill_tput/ISL, decode_goodput = decode_tput/OSL → P:D = (ISL/OSL) × (decode_tput / prefill_tput). Decode side comes from the calculator's own stepTime, auto-honoring regime, KV cap, SLO cap, and MoE corrections. Direction note: higher prefill MFU → faster prefill chips → FEWER prefill per decode. Splitwise A100→H100 controlled experiment (55→35 prefill machines, same workload) falsifies the older multiplicative MFU_p/MFU_d form.

formulas.name: Empirical sweep grids
formulas.description: Three grids: two server-side (Cartesian product, each combo = vLLM restart) and one client-side load axis. Brackets the analytical knee so the empirical sweep finds the actual cliff on either side.
formulas.derivation: Reference §0.5 two-stage methodology: min(b_slo, b_kv) rules out ~80% of the search space; tight sweep around it costs ~70 runs vs ~600 blind. max_num_seqs walks powers of 2 in [b/4, 2b] (vLLM scheduler is opinionated about them — Sarathi §4) to locate the empirical KV/SLO ceiling. max_num_batched_tokens draws from SARATHI_BANDS (shared with the picker — prevents drift where the picker recommends 1536 but the grid only shows {512,1024,2048,4096}), capped at 2× the picker's pick and at SARATHI_STRICT_CAP under strict TBT. concurrency uses fractional steps — deliberately NOT powers of 2 — to land at sub-saturation (TBT flat, throughput linear), at-knee (plateau), and super-saturation (TBT cliff, queue growth). If the cliff lands at 0.5b or 3b, the model is mis-calibrated for that workload.
